title: Cross-kind collision check references api_names that may not include all API seat names

finding.claim: Cross-kind collision check references api_names that may not include all API seat names
finding.recommendation: Populate api_names across all spec types before the agent finalization loop, or validate after both passes complete.

code_region.text:
candidate = base if n == 1 else f"{base}-{n}"
        while True:
            # Cross-kind and uniqueness checks compare on the
            # canonical (lowercased) name: seat identity is
            # case-insensitive, so an agent named 'Bot' must not
            # slip past an API seat named 'bot' (review-v11
            # finding — the custom-spec branch above once kept
            # its case while preset names were lowered).
            if candidate.lower() in api_names:
                raise ProviderError(
                    f"seat name {candidate!r} is used by both an "
                    f"agent seat and an API seat; rename the agent "
                    f"seat (e.g. agent:{base}-cli:<command>)")
            if candidate.lower() not in used:
                break
            candidate = _bump_name(candidate)
        used.add(candidate.lower())
        agent_final[idx] = candidate
    seats = {}
    counts = {}
    name_kind = {}

refutation.reason: The code populates `api_names` in a full first pass over all non-agent specs before the agent finalization loop runs, so the collision check does include all API seat names from the provided specs.

probe.summary: P12 executed (`probes/gap_providers_probe.py`, result `gap-providers-cluster.txt`, collision section) — `build_providers` over spec-order permutations at HEAD: - `agent:gemini` vs preset `gemini`, **both orders** → ProviderError (cross-kind), both times - `agent:myapi` vs custom `myapi|…` spec, **both orders** → ProviderError, both times - Case-folding: `agent:Gemini` vs `gemini`, and `agent:gemini` vs `Gemini` → ProviderError (comparison is on the canonical lowercased name) - Control (no collision): `agent:worker` + `gemini` builds both seats No order hides an API name from the check, because there is no interleaving to exploit: name collection is a complete first pass.
